frames.observation: The fresh exact-source opening frame shows the complete authored face, coat, hands and legs in native combat idle at HP 58. The retained native hat and knife remain attached.
The native robbery proficiency lifts the intact authored body into its forward attack pose. A bright native effect and the foreground hero obscure some lower-body detail.
After the proficiency, Thistlewick returns upright with the face, coat and limbs connected. The native result shows 20 hero damage and robbed gold while Thistlewick remains at HP 58.
The authored body becomes uniformly translucent during the native flee transition while still at HP 58. This is removal behavior and is not a death pose.
A native smoke cloud occupies the enemy slot after the full-health renderer is disabled. The encounter is ending through flee behavior; no death animation is claimed.
The retained ordinary no-focus hit begins the native heavy-damage recoil. The original body remains connected, although the hero, weapon and damage text overlap it.
The later recoil frame shows the target at HP 48 after the ordinary 58 to 48 hit. The coat, face and limbs remain coherent behind strong hero occlusion.
The same nonlethal-hit process later captures the native robbery attack. The authored silhouette remains connected, with the foreground hero limiting fine review.

conclusion: The exact custom renderer is coherent in native idle, ordinary nonlethal heavy-damage recoil, native robbery attack, recovery and the full-health flee transition. The renderer identity and 36-bone signature stay unchanged while present. Native flee is not death; V2 separately supplies explicit animated death evidence.
